speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me when these symptoms of double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness began, and whether you have noticed any drooping eyelids or slurred speech.

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The pattern of symptoms—ocular diplopia on gaze, ptosis, and fluctuating proximal weakness that worsens with exertion and improves with rest—is classic for this autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder. I recommend requesting a Tensilon test or Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody assay to confirm.
